Graph analysis: grand tour

Five bounded implementation slices are checkpointed. Graph layers now expose prerequisite foundations, typed multi-hop connections, structural families and source-backed dense overviews. Directed drawing shares geometry with inspection.

For integrated developer review · Branch feat/game-design-workbench · Implementation head 422f84385036e72bd770dd3acf32bf6ae6cb00f8

Ready for integrated review, not a completion or release claim

Kernel, CLI, compilation and rendering checks pass. Real-control activation, input isolation, reading usefulness and whole-branch rights/history approval remain open. Resource routes and composed outcomes are still not implemented.

Result and review boundary

The independent implementation assignment is delivered through a reviewable set of local commits. This report covers the five new slices and carries forward the earlier shared-neighbor, rooted-path and paired-witness work needed to understand them. Broad tasks in todo.md remain open where acceptance or wider scope is incomplete.

Read the layers without conflating them

All analysis uses the shown projection. Filters, relation roles and inactive-link visibility affect scope; camera, positions and clipping do not. Source identities, statuses, arrows, cycles and existing diagnostics stay visible. New layers are independently switchable and default off.

Encodings describe topology, not gameplay truth
EncodingMeaningNot a claim of
S / shared-neighbor purpleOther nodes sharing a shown incident identity; Any, Same role or Changed role lens. Branch comparison adds shared/A-only/B-only/excluded-role classes.Semantic equivalence or common gameplay purpose.

Partial discovery cannot prove absence. Completed local rows can remain useful under partial global discovery; unfinished closure rows cannot. Shape work exhaustion suppresses families entirely. Missing declarations remain outside shown scope, not invented links or automatically supplied knowledge.

Shared foundations, separate required branches

Question: which prerequisites recur across skills, and what additional branches remain required? The new F layer computes strict prerequisite closures, excluding each origin even in cycles. AND counts deduplicate direct identities without deleting authored redundant branches. Boundary uncertainty propagates through dependencies; cycles stay cycles, not grounded leaves.

Skills traverses incoming prerequisite-to-dependent presentation edges. Relationships follows authored dependent-to-prerequisite declarations. Challenges, matrix, MDA and Resources explicitly report prerequisite analysis unavailable rather than secretly analyzing a hidden skill graph.

Try: Skills → enable Prerequisite foundations layer → select jump-stomp → inspect shared-foundation peers and closure evidence. Choose fall-stomp for the branch comparison above. Automatic peer nomination uses deterministic projected order, not a quality ranking.

Existing constituent/combination opportunity and two-state route witnesses remain separate. A dependency closure neither adds knowledge nor demonstrates teaching quality. Source: gd_graph_closure.c, gd_graph_foundations_panel; implementation 065f47ab09c64bb5c470777f2832d690ebd36861.

Drawing follows source paths

Four deterministic rational barycentre sweeps reorder within unchanged semantic bands. Measured native label bounds and explicit card sizes reserve lanes. Directed settling no longer applies generic edge springs that collapse those lanes. Rank, prerequisite depth, entry hops, cycles and unplaced shelves retain their meanings.

Native Skills, Challenges and Relationships now share one polyline route for source lines, arrowheads, analysis underlays, field labels, Fit and hit testing. Adjacent gaps, long/feedback side corridors, parallel/opposite lanes and self-loops are explicit. A rendered detour does not leave an invisible selectable endpoint chord. MDA keeps its card/Bezier renderer; Resources keeps incidence lines.

Observed visual limits remain

The full plumber MDA graph fits a long mechanics band into the viewport, leaving tiny labels. Full-scope Resource cards overlap. Large parallel bundles, dragged-node obstacles and stacked badges still need active reading review. This is bounded ordering/routing, not a complete obstacle solver or measured readability improvement.

Source: gd_layout_directed.h, gd_layout_routes.c, gd_graph_view.c. Implementation 1df70dd5c7e42c4fe1f7e12feb0ac632391c6614. Initial old root-column test failed; a rendered-route false-incidence regression replaced the obsolete coordinate expectation, then the full suite passed.

Mandatory paths and one bypass witness

Earlier checkpoint work stays available. Fixed analysis starts never follow inspection selection. Challenges uses shown authored entries; other adapters need explicit starts. No starts means unavailable. A visibly synthetic multi-entry root is analysis-only, never an authored encounter or learning state.

Mandatory paths layer uses iterative reverse-postorder fixed-point dominators. D counts other reachable dominated targets; ! marks mandatory ancestors; J is a join/loop candidate count, not a reconvergence proof. Pink is one support path. Unreachable nodes show D−; unfinished dominators expose no intermediate proof.

Compare support / bypass nominates nonmandatory candidates on that one support path. Cyan retains one candidate-avoiding witness. F/R delimit internally vertex-disjoint branches while respecting both witness orders, including cyclic order differences. Separate-start F is disclosed as virtual. No candidate here does not establish no alternatives elsewhere.

Directed paths are shown topology, not physical reachability. Matrix/Resource adapters report necessary incidence connections, not flow. Skill path domination is not AND prerequisite necessity. Broader reconvergence discovery and cross-view/manual acceptance remain open.

Implementations: rooted paths b898efd; paired witnesses 301ccdeea77a08877dea23d52b71f42dedf7292e. Source: gd_graph_paths.c, shared path panel and renderer adapters. Tests cover 1,536 independent vertex-removal projections and all nominated candidates, cycles, multiple/hidden starts, budgets, suffixes and reload-root remapping.

Typed multi-hop discovery, not another AND engine

One chosen link kind and explicit traversal orientation define ordinary reachability. T reuse counts expose graph-wide reached identities before pair drill-down. Automatic shared-target peers and full shared/A-only/B-only graph marks retain source indices; deterministic BFS supplies a bounded displayed witness suffix.

Try: enable Typed multi-hop layer; choose a relation kind; inspect Shown arrows or Against shown arrows; expand peers/evidence. Reversing traversal never reverses source arrows. Matrix/Resources always disclose same-kind undirected incidence. Mixed semantic joins are not silently inferred.

Parameter/projection changes reset derived peer/target nominations; camera changes do not. Incomplete global T counts are lower bounds. Completed local rows can still support exact comparisons, but unfinished rows cannot prove no connection. Text retains at most 64 trailing witness arcs, in reverse storage order; full length remains separate.

Source: generic gd_graph_closure_into, gd_graph_closure_path, gd_graph_reachability_ui.c. Implementation d762c9f0783069ecebd6e5e5cc78634affc5badd. Existing 384 independent closure cases also validate completed pair/target witness reachability, source direction, scope and retained suffix continuity.

Exact local shape families

Two refinement rounds start from projected node roles. Each signature includes the previous node class and a sorted multiset of relation-kind, endpoint-role and previous-neighbor-class tuples. Exact comparisons determine families; no unchecked hash equality or learned score. Duplicate declarations deduplicate before signatures, while distinct same-colored neighbors retain multiplicity.

Try: enable Structural shape families layer → open Discovered shape families → choose a representative → inspect Shape signature and members. Family ID/size badges appear graph-wide; a gold outer outline marks selected family. IDs are transient per projection/reload, not persistent source identity.

Missing data can change families; rare shapes are not defects. Work exhaustion suppresses all family claims instead of exposing intermediate classes. Complete families can survive truncated shared-pair discovery because signatures use the full shown incident feature index. Richer branch-semantic comparisons and usefulness validation remain open.

Source: gd_graph_shapes.c, GD_GraphShapes, shared family panel and three renderer adapters. Implementation 69ff0e6b56c82ccb260edb0ed59db14eb1f6880f; snapshot-member correction 422f84385036e72bd770dd3acf32bf6ae6cb00f8. Independent pairwise-interning oracle covers 128 small projections, with permutation, direction, role, multiplicity, budget, isolate and full 65,536-feature cases.

Dense overview with source-backed cells

The optional fixed-screen inset retains every shown identity in at most 32×32 contiguous projection-index bins. These are presentation bins, not semantic clusters. Camera and positions do not alter membership. Directed rows follow shown arrows; matrix/Resources mirror incidence across different bins. Total input rows count each original projected row once.

Brightness uses logarithmic bands of link-row count, not strength, quantity or flow width. Parallel projected rows remain separate. A diagonal aggregate can contain links between different nodes inside one bin; it is not self-loop proof. Derived noun/verb matrix rows remain derived rows, not newly invented declarations.

Try: enable Adjacency / incidence overview; click a cell or use Row bin, Column bin, Inspect bin cell. Gold underlays/outlines identify actual contributing edges/endpoints, not every member of either bin. Source evidence includes identity ranges/examples, typed counts and projected provenance. Source-link text caps are separate from complete cell counts/brush flags.

Resources cycles its Layers header through Foundations → Typed paths → Shapes → Overview. It also offers row/column cycling, Next occupied cell, Clear cell and arrow-key movement. Inset pointer/wheel/pan input blocks the underlying graph; entering it stops an ongoing node drag. That behavior is implemented and code-reviewed, but real-pointer acceptance remains unverified.

Source: gd_graph_overview.c, gd_graph_overview_draw.h and shared inspector. Implementation 8c8eead8a56bc8f4dca8bc02c46a3a1b879c3de3. Every cell/count/first-source/brush flag is checked across 64 independent masked/active/directed/incidence projections, including full capacity and exact results despite partial pair discovery.

Decision history and bounded revision paths

Implementation choices below were delegated while the user was away. They remain provisional engineering defaults, not settled product requirements. Alternatives are those recorded during the work; no unrun bake-off or performance advantage is implied.

Plan before code; checkpoint safe steps

Question: how to keep independent delivery reviewable? Chose one written plan and commit per coherent step in the dedicated worktree. Planning commit 5b4dbd28a9e052c3c63c8e18c9c4d7a257d0fe6a, starting at 301ccde. Repeated manual slice gates were not used because integrated review was delegated. No alternate worker/integration scheme was adopted. Revise sequencing in the plan; do not rewrite history or touch another worktree.

Strict prerequisite closure with bounded bitsets

Step 1, commit 065f47ab09c64bb5c470777f2832d690ebd36861. Graph-wide reuse needs all-origin traversal; retained fixed bitset rows after measuring 2,826,320 bytes/cache, including 2,097,152 bytes of bitsets. A single-source BFS is cheaper for one query; no speed benefit was measured. Bitsets bound selected-peer intersection to 4,096×64 words. Keep storage outside model/draft/reload snapshots. Revisit for memory pressure or representative query measurements; change GD_GraphClosure internals and oracle tests together, retaining strict roots, boundary/cycle flags and completed-row semantics.

Preserve bands; bound crossing work and routing

Step 2, commit 1df70dd5c7e42c4fe1f7e12feb0ac632391c6614. Chose four rational barycentre sweeps and explicit native polylines. Did not collapse SCCs into fake records, assign new semantic ranks, iterate to a claimed crossing optimum or build a complete obstacle solver. MDA/Resource renderer specialization remains. Evidence is deterministic geometry tests, not a comprehension benchmark. Revisit concrete long-label, feedback, parallel-bundle or drag failures in gd_layout_directed.h/gd_layout_routes.c; retain common render/hit/arrow geometry and source keys.

Separate AND dependency from ordinary reachability

Step 3, commit d762c9f0783069ecebd6e5e5cc78634affc5badd. Reused closure machinery in independent caches instead of one mutually exclusive semantic mode or a second opportunity engine. One explicit relation kind/direction avoids inventing mixed MDA/resource joins. Costs a second 2,826,320-byte cache; allows independent layers. Revisit only with a useful mixed-kind contract and sourced examples. Extend typed projection policy/witnesses first; do not repurpose F or expand known skills.

Two exact refinement rounds, not embeddings

Step 4, commit 69ff0e6b56c82ccb260edb0ed59db14eb1f6880f. Chose exact tuple comparison/merge ordering and role-seeded two-round families, not hash-only equality, unbounded stabilization or rainbow community authority. Tests establish the defined partition, not usefulness. False semantic similarities are expected outside this local structural definition. Revisit after real comparison tasks; change round/signature policy explicitly in gd_graph_shapes.c and independent oracle. Preserve member identity and label limitations; do not turn rarity into a defect score.

Optional index bins, not flow or semantic clusters

Step 5, commit 8c8eead8a56bc8f4dca8bc02c46a3a1b879c3de3. Chose ≤32×32 bins over all shown identities, log-banded input-row counts and original contributor brushing. No arbitrary automatic size switch, flow widths, source topology collapse or parallel-row deduplication. Bin order is reproducible but not semantically meaningful; overlay can occlude detail. Revisit for a demonstrated reading task in gd_graph_overview.c/gd_graph_overview_draw.h; preserve exact scope/count/provenance and input isolation. Quantity-based flow requires a different contract.

Rendering probes are not control acceptance

Validation, commit 422f84385036e72bd770dd3acf32bf6ae6cb00f8. Used fresh private source copies with initialized layer/selection state instead of OS input automation. This safely exercises rendering while leaving real-control acceptance open; it is not a workaround establishing denied owned-window interaction. Added snapshot-local member keys after repeated Resource labels obscured distinct identities. Revisit controls through integrated manual review, not by relabeling capture success. Rebuild with scripts/capture-workbench-graph-review.ps1; production sources/examples are hash-checked, explorer drafts must stay empty.

Dependencies: typed reachability reuses closure machinery; family signatures reuse the canonical incident feature index; overviews reuse raw projected rows rather than truncated discovered pairs. A bounded revision should target those components and matching adapters/tests, not blindly revert a multi-file checkpoint.

Checks that failed, were skipped or remain unrun

  • Old drawing root-column assertion failed during development; stronger rendered-path false-incidence test replaced it and full suite passed. This was not an accepted crash or suppressed test failure.
  • Full Zig debug linking lacked cached crt2.obj/MinGW libraries. Strict Zig compilation and CJIT executable builds/tests pass; that is not a passed Zig-link check.
  • Four Node external integrations skipped for unavailable Attendant/desktop inputs.
  • Historical owned probes refused activation or foreground ownership. No global-input workaround; expanded evidence and Resource paired comparison were not accepted.
  • New layer controls, multi-layer combinations, live source refresh after these layers, actual cell-brush input isolation and reading usefulness need manual review. Rendering probes do not close those gates.
  • No benchmark, player study, experiment rerun or claim of balance, teaching quality, economy correctness or improved comprehension.

Integrated walkthrough and next decisions

  1. Small directed graph first. Open crate Skills. Follow source arrows and inspect the existing orange rank conflict; switch depth/rank/orientation, Fit and zoom. Check routed path hits, not old endpoint chords.
  2. AND versus shared foundation. In plumber Skills select jump-stomp, enable F, choose fall-stomp from discovered peers. Read shared trunk and every extra required branch. Confirm no known skill is added; inspect constituent versus combination opportunities separately.
  3. Focused scope. In Relationships, inspect authored arrows and boundary count. Expand explicitly; verify F/T/shape/overview recompute only for newly shown scope. Pan/zoom should not change counts.
  4. Fixed starts and bypass. In crate Challenges enable Mandatory paths and Compare support / bypass; inspect combined-room and switch-practice. Check starts stay fixed, pink/cyan preserve source styles, and F/R match source witness order.
  5. Typed discovery. Choose a kind/direction, inspect a discovered peer and witness target. Check reversed traversal is disclosed, source arrows do not flip, and no-incidence-match is not an AND verdict.
  6. Shape usefulness. Compare distinct isolated mechanic records in crate MDA. Inspect member references and full signature counts. Decide whether the lens helps a real question without treating same local family as same gameplay.
  7. Dense cell provenance. In both matrix and Resources select occupied/empty/diagonal cells. Verify counts and source examples; unrelated bin members must not gain contributor outlines.
  8. Input isolation. Click, drag, pan and wheel inside inset; underlying nodes/camera must not respond. Enter inset during a node drag. Toggle layer off and verify ordinary graph input resumes.
  9. Independent layers and reload. Combine then disable F/T/families/overview; examine stacked marks and legends. Change filters; verify derived peer/cell selections reset. Recheck drafts, undo and last-good refresh without using source edits as test acceptance shortcuts.
  10. Whole-branch review. Review history, imported references/vendor rights and unresolved task scope before any merge/public release. Do not close resource routing, composed outcomes or broad discovery/reconvergence umbrellas from these bounded slices.

Proposed follow-up, not a new requirement: use failures from that walkthrough to refine labels/navigation and family/overview usefulness before introducing richer semantic joins, more rounds, embeddings or resource-route simulation.
